title: Iowa Cyclospora Cases Hit 226 as Nationwide Outbreak Tops 6,700 Infections
excerpt: Iowa has confirmed 226 cyclosporiasis cases across 48 counties in 2026, a sharp spike from 69 cases in all of 2025, as a massive national outbreak linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce continues to spread.
body:
• Iowa has confirmed 226 cyclosporiasis cases in 48 counties as of July 30, more than triple the 69 cases reported in all of 2025.
  • Nationally, more than 6,700 cases have been logged across 45 states since May 1, with 423 hospitalizations and no deaths.
  • The largest outbreak cluster is linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico served at Taco Bell locations; a recall was issued on July 17.
  • Experts warn case counts will continue to rise due to the parasite's long incubation period of up to a month.

Iowa's cyclosporiasis cases have surged to 226 across 48 counties as of July 30, according to the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services — a dramatic increase from the 69 cases the state recorded in all of 2025. The spike comes amid an unprecedented national outbreak of the parasitic infection that has now sickened more than 6,700 people in 45 states.

Not all of Iowa's cases are connected to the ongoing national outbreak investigations, however. Of the 226 confirmed infections, 47 patients reported recent international travel, meaning they likely contracted the parasite abroad, HHS Communications Director Danielle Sample said in a statement.

A National Crisis Centered on Iceberg Lettuce

The CDC reported more than 2,500 new cases in its weekly update released on July 28, bringing the national total to over 6,700 confirmed infections with 423 hospitalizations. No deaths have been reported.

https://x.com/ShiningScience/status/2082639614276149444

Federal health authorities are investigating what they believe to be multiple separate outbreaks. The largest cluster — involving 1,947 confirmed cases across nine states — has been traced to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico served at Taco Bell locations in Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia.

Michigan has been hit hardest, reporting 6,148 cases and 102 hospitalizations — dwarfing the 40 to 50 cases the state typically sees in a year, according to Medscape. Ohio has tallied 1,246 cases, Indiana 427, and West Virginia 139.

"I've been a little concerned that there was possibly more than one source for this outbreak."

— Cynthia L. Sears, MD, Professor of Medicine, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine

Taylor Farms Recall and Taco Bell Response

On July 17, Taylor Farms de Mexico voluntarily recalled all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico. The recall covers Marketside-brand products sold at Walmart — including 12-ounce and 24-ounce Iceberg Salad and 8-ounce and 16-ounce Shredded Lettuce — with best-by dates ranging from July 18 to August 3, 2026. The recalled products were distributed to food service customers across 27 states, according to the FDA.

Taco Bell confirmed it stopped using lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico as of July 17. FDA's traceback investigation identified convergence on a single supplier of shredded iceberg lettuce used by Taco Bell locations where sick people ate before becoming ill.

FDA Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantis said in a July 20 briefing that the agency had investigated "five different subclusters" of cyclosporiasis and concluded three of the inquiries. He noted that cyclosporiasis is a "seasonal hazard," with cases typically concentrated from May through August, and that more than 4,500 cases were reported nationally in 2023 and 3,500 in 2024.

Diagnostic Challenges and Treatment

Infectious disease specialists are urging clinicians to maintain a high index of suspicion for cyclosporiasis, even in states that have not declared outbreaks.

"Even in states that have not declared an outbreak, if someone is presenting with frequent watery diarrhea, the suspicion for cyclosporiasis should be high, just given the scope of how big this outbreak is."

— Nahid Bhadelia, MD, Founding Director, Boston University Center on Emerging Infectious Diseases

The Cyclospora parasite causes watery diarrhea, cramping, nausea, fatigue, and weight loss. Symptoms can appear two days to two weeks after infection and may come and go — unlike typical food poisoning. The infection is treatable with a 7- to 10-day course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, though neither that antibiotic nor the backup option, ciprofloxacin, is safe during pregnancy.

Clinicians must specifically request that stool samples be tested for the parasite, as standard testing panels often do not include it. Older patients, children, immunocompromised individuals, and pregnant women face higher risks from fluid loss and complications.

What to Watch For

Experts expect case numbers to keep climbing despite the recall. The parasite's long incubation period — up to a month from infection to illness — means cases from exposures before the July 17 recall will continue to surface for weeks.

The FDA said its investigation remains ongoing and that additional implicated brands, restaurants, retailers, or distribution channels may be identified. Consumers who purchased recalled iceberg lettuce are advised to discard it immediately and sanitize any surfaces it touched. Anyone experiencing prolonged watery diarrhea, especially after eating shredded iceberg lettuce in the past two weeks, should contact their healthcare provider and specifically request Cyclospora testing.
nri_angle: Indians in the U.S., particularly those in affected Midwestern states, should avoid recalled iceberg lettuce products and seek medical testing for Cyclospora if experiencing prolonged diarrhea.
